overview: One confirms a protein you already suspect is there; the other can discover proteins you never thought to look for.
genZNote: One confirms a protein you already suspect. One finds proteins you didn't know to look for.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Detects a specific, pre-selected protein using an antibody after separating proteins by size via gel electrophoresis and transferring them to a membrane.
aspects.valueB: Identifies and quantifies proteins by measuring the mass-to-charge ratio of peptide fragments, matching the resulting spectra against protein databases.

aspects.label: Targeted vs Untargeted Approach
aspects.valueA: Targeted — requires a specific antibody against the protein of interest, decided in advance.
aspects.valueB: Can be untargeted (discovery proteomics), identifying hundreds to thousands of proteins in a sample without prior selection.

aspects.label: Dependence on Antibody Quality
aspects.valueA: Entirely dependent on antibody specificity and quality; cross-reactivity can cause false results.
aspects.valueB: No antibody required — identification is based on measured peptide mass and sequence matching.

aspects.label: Quantitative Precision
aspects.valueA: Semi-quantitative at best, based on band intensity relative to a loading control.
aspects.valueB: Can achieve precise, often absolute quantification, especially with labeled internal standards.

aspects.label: Throughput and Scale
aspects.valueA: Low throughput — one or a few proteins per membrane, run individually.
aspects.valueB: High throughput — capable of profiling an entire proteome in a single run.

aspects.label: Equipment and Cost
aspects.valueA: Relatively inexpensive and widely accessible standard lab equipment.
aspects.valueB: Requires expensive, specialized mass spectrometry instrumentation and dedicated bioinformatics expertise.

aspects.label: Typical Applications
aspects.valueA: Confirming expression or knockdown of a specific known protein.
aspects.valueB: Discovery proteomics, post-translational modification mapping, biomarker discovery studies.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Antibody-based detection of one known protein at a time.
aspects.valueB: Mass-based identification/quantification of many proteins at once, no antibody needed.
